key_insight: Entrance-generated vortices create geometry-specific temperature-polarization bias whose magnitude and direction change with inlet Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: Lab-scale membrane characterization and heat-transfer correlations must account for entrance geometry and flow conditions rather than apply a constant correction.
method: Performed 3D CFD simulations of direct contact membrane distillation.
Varied inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000.
Examined side-chamber length and main-channel height against a straight-channel baseline.
evidence_signal: Simulations found entrance vortices across all geometries, with greater downstream persistence at higher Reynolds numbers; most geometries shifted from stronger polarization than the baseline at low Reynolds numbers to weaker polarization at high Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational results without experimental validation, so transfer to other module designs requires verification.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
